questions.question_english: Under the constitutional framework of Articles 15(6) and 16(6), is a State Government legally permitted to implement EWS reservation in state public employment while modifying the family income ceiling from Rs. 8 Lakh to Rs. 6 Lakh?
options_english: No, because Central DoPT guidelines are mandatory, uniform, and legally binding on all state governments
Yes, because State Governments possess constitutional autonomy to determine eligibility criteria for state civil posts and admissions
Yes, but only after Parliament passes a special resolution approving the state's deviation
No, because the Rs. 8 Lakh income ceiling is explicitly enshrined in the text of the Constitution of India
questions.explanation_english: Articles 15(6) and 16(6) of the Constitution of India, inserted by the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, explicitly state that 'economically weaker sections' shall be such as may be notified by the 'State' from time to time on the basis of family income and other indicators of economic disadvantage. Under Article 12, the term 'State' includes both the Union Government and State Governments/Legislatures. While the Central Government notified the Rs. 8 Lakh ceiling for central civil posts and Central Educational Institutions, State Governments retain the constitutional authority and administrative competence under their respective legislative and executive powers (Entries 41 and 25 of List II and List III) to fix or modify the income and asset criteria for employment under the State and state-run institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi: 103वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2019 द्वारा जोड़े गए भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 15(6) और 16(6) के स्पष्टीकरण (Explanation) में कहा गया है कि 'आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्ग' वे होंगे जिन्हें पारिवारिक आय और आर्थिक प्रतिकूलता के अन्य संकेतकों के आधार पर 'राज्य' द्वारा समय-समय पर अधिसूचित किया जाएगा। अनुच्छेद 12 के अंतर्गत 'राज्य' में राज्य सरकारें भी शामिल हैं। केंद्र सरकार द्वारा निर्धारित 8 लाख रुपये की सीमा केंद्रीय सेवाओं और संस्थानों के लिए है। राज्य सरकारों को अपने राज्य के अधीन पदों और राज्य संस्थानों में EWS आरक्षण लागू करने हेतु आय सीमा (जैसे 6 लाख रुपये) या परिसंपत्ति मानदंडों को स्वतंत्र रूप से अधिसूचित या संशोधित करने का पूर्ण संवैधानिक अधिकार प्राप्त है।

questions.question_english: In the constitution of the School Management Committee (SMC) under Section 21 of the RTE Act, 2009, which of the following groups must be given proportionate representation among the parent members based on their population in the neighborhood?
options_english: Women members residing in the locality
questions.explanation_english: Section 21 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 governs the establishment and composition of the School Management Committee (SMC). The law mandates that at least three-fourths (75%) of the members of such a committee shall be parents or guardians of children admitted in the school, and 50% of the committee members must be women. Crucially, the second proviso to Section 21(1) explicitly states: 'Provided further that proportionate representation shall be given to the parents or guardians of children belonging to disadvantaged group and weaker section'. Furthermore, representation must reflect the demographic proportion of Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in that neighborhood. This democratic safeguard guarantees that marginalized communities have a direct voice in school development plans, fund monitoring, and mid-day meal oversight.
questions.explanation_hindi: आरटीई (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 21 के अनुसार प्रत्येक सरकारी व सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालय में विद्यालय प्रबंधन समिति (SMC) का गठन अनिवार्य है। इस धारा के अनुसार कुल सदस्यों में से कम से कम 75% सदस्य विद्यार्थियों के माता-पिता या अभिभावक होंगे तथा 50% सदस्य महिलाएं होंगी। धारा 21(1) के दूसरे परंतुक (Proviso) में यह विशेष प्रावधान है कि अलाभित समूह (Disadvantaged Group) और कमजोर वर्ग (Weaker Section) के बच्चों के माता-पिता/अभिभावकों को विद्यालय के परिक्षेत्र (पड़ोस) में उनकी जनसंख्या के अनुपात में प्रतिनिधित्व दिया जाएगा। इसमें अनुसूचित जातियों (SC) और अनुसूचित जनजातियों (ST) का आनुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व सुनिश्चित करना सांविधिक रूप से अनिवार्य है ताकि विद्यालय के निर्णयों और प्रबंधन में हाशिए के वर्गों की सक्रिय भागीदारी हो सके। अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: Under Section 32 of the RPwD Act, 2016, all government institutions of higher education and other higher educational institutions receiving aid from the Government are required to reserve what minimum percentage of seats for persons with benchmark disabilities?
questions.explanation_english:
Section 32(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 explicitly provides:
'All Government institutions of higher education and other higher education institutions receiving aid from the Government shall reserve not less than five per cent seats for persons with benchmark disabilities.'

Candidates often confuse this with employment reservation: under Section 34 of the Act, reservation in public sector employment is set at a minimum of 4%, whereas under Section 32, reservation in government and government-aided institutions of higher education is set at not less than 5%. Furthermore, Section 32(2) provides an upper age relaxation of 5 years for admission to such higher educational institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 32(1) स्पष्ट रूप से यह अधिदेशित करती है:
'उच्च शिक्षा के सभी सरकारी संस्थान और सरकार से सहायता प्राप्त अन्य उच्च शिक्षा संस्थान बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाले व्यक्तियों के लिए कम से कम पांच प्रतिशत (5%) सीटें आरक्षित करेंगे।'

ध्यान रहे कि सार्वजनिक रोजगार में धारा 34 के तहत बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगजनों के लिए न्यूनतम 4% आरक्षण का प्रावधान है, जबकि उच्च शिक्षण संस्थानों (महाविद्यालयों/विश्वविद्यालयों) में प्रवेश हेतु धारा 32 के तहत यह कोटा 'न्यूनतम 5%' निर्धारित किया गया है। इसके अतिरिक्त धारा 32(2) के तहत उच्च शिक्षा में प्रवेश के लिए अधिकतम आयु सीमा में 5 वर्ष की छूट का भी वैधानिक प्रावधान है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) 5%

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 32 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 mandates that all government institutions of higher education and institutions receiving government aid must reserve a minimum of five percent of available seats for persons with benchmark disabilities. This provision aims to promote higher educational attainment and career development opportunities for disabled students nationwide.

questions.question_english: The Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) students is specifically applicable to students studying in which classes?
questions.explanation_english: The Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-Matric Scholarship for SC Students (administered by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment) and ST Students (administered by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs) is specifically targeted at students studying in Classes IX and X. Under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, elementary education (Classes I to VIII) is already free in government and government-aided schools. Consequently, the critical juncture where disadvantaged SC/ST students experience high dropout rates due to financial constraints is during secondary transition. The Pre-Matric scholarship scheme provides financial grants, academic allowances, and tuition assistance during Classes IX and X to prevent attrition, improve retention, and enable students to successfully pass the matriculation board examination.
questions.explanation_hindi: सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय तथा जनजातीय कार्य मंत्रालय द्वारा संचालित अनुसूचित जाति (SC) और अनुसूचित जनजाति (ST) के छात्रों के लिए केंद्र प्रायोजित 'प्री-मैट्रिक छात्रवृत्ति योजना' विशेष रूप से 'कक्षा IX और X' (कक्षा 9 और 10) के विद्यार्थियों के लिए लागू है। शिक्षा का अधिकार (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 के तहत कक्षा I से VIII तक की प्रारंभिक शिक्षा सरकारी स्कूलों में पहले से ही पूर्णतः निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य है। अतः माध्यमिक स्तर (कक्षा 9वीं और 10वीं) में प्रवेश करते समय वंचित वर्ग के छात्रों में होने वाले स्कूल छोड़ने (ड्रॉपआउट) की दर को रोकने तथा उन्हें मैट्रिक बोर्ड परीक्षा सफलतापूर्वक उत्तीर्ण कराने के उद्देश्य से यह छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान की जाती है। कक्षा XI और XII की छात्रवृत्ति 'पोस्ट-मैट्रिक' योजना के अंतर्गत आती है।

questions.question_english: Under the Central Government EWS reservation guidelines, ownership of a residential plot of what minimum area in a notified municipality automatically disqualifies a family from claiming EWS status?
questions.explanation_english: Under the DoPT OM dated 31st January 2019 laying down the asset criteria for EWS reservations, ownership of a residential plot of 100 square yards and above in notified municipalities serves as an absolute disqualification. questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The RPwD Act, 2016 mandates that the appropriate Government shall ensure that persons with disabilities enjoy the right to equality and a life with dignity.
Reason (R): The Act prohibits the deprivation of personal liberty of any person solely on the ground of disability.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both statements are correct statutory provisions under the RPwD Act, 2016, but Reason (R) is not the causal explanation of Assertion (A). Section 3(1) of the Act mandates that the appropriate Government shall ensure that persons with disabilities enjoy the right to equality, life with dignity, and respect for their integrity equally with others, directly giving effect to Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution. Meanwhile, Section 4(1) provides that no person shall be deprived of his or her personal liberty only on the ground of disability. Although both are statutory rights safeguarding dignity and freedom, the prohibition against deprivation of personal liberty is an independent legal guarantee under Section 4 and does not logically or causally explain why the State must ensure equality and dignity under Section 3.

questions.question_english: In constitutional and service jurisprudence, reservation provided for SC, ST, and OBC is classified as "Vertical Reservation". What is reservation provided for special target groups such as Women, Ex-Servicemen, and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) classified as?
questions.explanation_english: Under Indian constitutional jurisprudence, established by the Nine-Judge Constitution Bench in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) and further explained in Rajesh Kumar Daria v. RPSC (2007), reservation is bifurcated into two distinct categories: (1) Vertical Reservation, which is provided in favor of socially and educationally backward classes under Article 16(4) (SCs, STs, and OBCs) and economically weaker sections under Article 16(6); and (2) Horizontal Reservation, which is provided under Article 16(1) and Article 15(3) for categories like Women, Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD, mandated under Section 34 of the RPwD Act, 2016), and Ex-Servicemen. Horizontal reservation cuts across vertical reservation (interlocking reservation), meaning beneficiaries are adjusted within their respective vertical social categories (UR, SC, ST, OBC, EWS).

Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Article 15(4) allows the State to provide fee concessions and scholarships exclusively to students from SC and ST communities without violating the Right to Equality.
Reason (R): Article 15(4) functions as a specific constitutional exception to the general rule of non-discrimination laid down in Article 15(1) and Article 29(2).

options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) is the direct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct: Under Article 15(4), the State regularly formulates targeted welfare measures such as post-matric scholarships, fee concessions, book bank facilities, and hostel fee waivers exclusively for students belonging to Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST). These targeted affirmative actions do not violate the Right to Equality (Article 14).
Reason (R) is correct: Article 15(1) prohibits discrimination against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth, and Article 29(2) bars denial of admission into state-funded institutions on similar grounds. Article 15(4) explicitly begins with a non-obstante clause ('Nothing in this article or in clause (2) of article 29 shall prevent the State...'), making it an express constitutional exception designed to achieve substantive equality. Because Article 15(4) carves out this specific exception, such targeted educational benefits and scholarships exclusively for SC and ST students are constitutionally immune from challenges alleging unlawful discrimination. Thus, R correctly explains A.

questions.question_english: Article 15(4) was inserted into the Constitution of India by which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts?
questions.explanation_english: Article 15(4) was inserted into the Constitution of India by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951. This historic amendment was introduced by Parliament under Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in response to the landmark Supreme Court decision in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951). In that case, the Supreme Court struck down the Madras Government's Communal G.O., which allocated college seats based on caste and community, holding that it violated Article 29(2). To safeguard state-sponsored affirmative action and educational reservations for marginalized communities, Parliament enacted Article 15(4) as an enabling clause. It provides that nothing in Article 15 or in Article 29(2) shall prevent the State from making any special provision for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens (SEBCs) or for the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
questions.explanation_hindi: भारतीय संविधान में अनुच्छेद 15(4) को संविधान (प्रथम संशोधन) अधिनियम, 1951 द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। यह ऐतिहासिक संशोधन संसद द्वारा सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के 'मद्रास राज्य बनाम चंपकम दोराइराजन (1951)' के ऐतिहासिक फैसले के परिणामस्वरूप लाया गया था। इस मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने मद्रास सरकार के उस 'कम्युनल जी.ओ.' को रद्द कर दिया था, जिसके तहत शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में जातियों और समुदायों के अनुसार सीटें आरक्षित की गई थीं, क्योंकि यह अनुच्छेद 29(2) का उल्लंघन करता था। पिछड़े वर्गों और वंचित समुदायों के लिए शैक्षणिक आरक्षण और सकारात्मक कदमों की संवैधानिक सुरक्षा हेतु संसद ने अनुच्छेद 15(4) को एक समर्थकारी उपबंध (enabling provision) के रूप में जोड़ा। यह उपबंध राज्य को सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्गों (SEBCs) अथवा अनुसूचित जातियों (SCs) और अनुसूचित जनजातियों (STs) की उन्नति के लिए विशेष प्रावधान करने का अधिकार देता है।

questions.question_english: In a small cadre consisting of 13 or fewer posts, what is the specialized replacement roster maintained under DoPT guidelines to ensure reservations are allocated without exceeding the constitutional 50% ceiling commonly known as?
questions.explanation_english: Under DoPT OM No. 36012/2/96-Estt (Res) dated 2nd July 1997, maintaining a standard 200-point roster in small cadres containing 1 to 13 posts would cause severe distortion and violate the 50% reservation ceiling laid down in Indra Sawhney. questions.question_english: A recognized private unaided minority school in Delhi is directed by the Directorate of Education to admit students from socially and educationally backward classes under a state quota policy. Can the school legally refuse?
options_english: No, because Article 15(5) completely overrides all constitutional minority rights

questions.explanation_english: A recognized private unaided minority educational institution can legally refuse to comply with state quota directives. Article 15(5) explicitly carves out an exception for minority educational institutions: 'other than the minority educational institutions referred to in clause (1) of article 30'. Furthermore, in Pramati Educational & Cultural Trust (2014), the Supreme Court ruled that state reservation mandates or quotas under the RTE Act cannot be imposed on minority institutions (aided or unaided) as that would infringe upon their constitutional autonomy under Article 30(1) to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. questions.explanation_english: Article 15(5) was inserted into the Constitution of India by the Constitution (Ninety-Third Amendment) Act, 2005, which took effect on 20 January 2006. questions.question_english: The Supreme Court of India has consistently applied the principle of harmonious construction between Directive Principles and Fundamental Rights, reading Article 46 alongside which constitutional provision to sustain affirmative action and special educational measures for SCs and STs?
questions.explanation_english:
The doctrine of harmonious construction is a foundational principle of Indian constitutional jurisprudence, establishing that Fundamental Rights (Part III) and Directive Principles (Part IV) must be construed together to achieve the constitutional goal of a welfare state.

Following the landmark ruling in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951 added clause (4) to Article 15. Article 15(4) enables the State to make 'any special provision for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens or for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.'

The Supreme Court has repeatedly held that Article 15(4) is an enabling provision designed to give effect to the directive principle enshrined in Article 46 (which obligates the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and weaker sections). By reading Article 46 alongside Article 15(4), the judiciary has upheld reservations in educational institutions, fee concessions, relaxation of qualifying marks, and special scholarship schemes against challenges alleging violations of formal equality under Article 15(1) or Article 29(2).
questions.explanation_hindi:
भारतीय संवैधानिक न्यायशास्त्र में सामंजस्यपूर्ण व्याख्या (harmonious construction) का सिद्धांत यह स्थापित करता है कि मौलिक अधिकार (भाग III) और नीति निर्देशक तत्व (भाग IV) एक-दूसरे के विरोधी नहीं, बल्कि पूरक हैं।

मद्रास राज्य बनाम चंपकम दोराइराजन (1951) के मामले के बाद प्रथम संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1951 द्वारा अनुच्छेद 15 में खंड (4) जोड़ा गया। अनुच्छेद 15(4) राज्य को 'सामाजिक और शैक्षिक दृष्टि से पिछड़े वर्गों की उन्नति के लिए या अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के लिए कोई विशेष उपबंध' करने की शक्ति प्रदान करता है।

सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने बार-बार यह निर्धारित किया है कि अनुच्छेद 15(4) वस्तुतः अनुच्छेद 46 में उल्लिखित नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांत (कमजोर वर्गों विशेषकर एससी और एसटी के शैक्षणिक व आर्थिक हितों की अभिवृद्धि) को क्रियान्वित करने का एक संवैधानिक साधन है। अनुच्छेद 46 और 15(4) को एक साथ पढ़कर ही शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में आरक्षण, शुल्क में छूट और विशेष छात्रवृत्तियों को समानता के अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 14 और 15(1)) के अनुरूप वैध ठहराया गया है।

questions.question_english: Under Section 32 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, if a parent from a disadvantaged group has a grievance regarding denial of admission, which designated authority serves as the primary statutory forum to receive and decide the grievance?
options_english: The High Court of the concerned State
The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
The Minister in charge of State Education
questions.explanation_english:
Section 32 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 sets up a clear decentralised grievance redressal framework:
1. Section 32(1) explicitly states: 'Notwithstanding anything contained in section 31, any person having any grievance relating to the right of a child under this Act may make a written complaint to the local authority having jurisdiction.' (In municipal areas, this is the Municipal Corporation/Municipality; in rural areas, it is the Panchayati Raj Institution/Block Education Office).
2. Section 32(2) mandates that after receiving the complaint, the Local Authority shall decide the matter within a period of three months after affording a reasonable opportunity of being heard to the parties concerned.
3. Section 32(3) provides that any person aggrieved by the decision of the local authority may prefer an appeal to the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR).
Therefore, the Local Authority is the designated first forum of receipt and adjudication.

questions.question_english: What does the term "Own Merit Candidate" (also known as Meritorious Reserved Candidate - MRC) mean in the context of government recruitment and post-based reservation rosters?
options_english: A reserved candidate selected on open merit without relaxed standards
A reserved candidate who receives a government merit scholarship for study
A candidate who successfully clears the competitive exam in their first attempt
A candidate applying exclusively for unreserved posts who forfeits caste benefits
questions.explanation_english: In constitutional law and service jurisprudence (reiterated in the landmark Indra Sawhney judgment and DoPT OM No. 36012/23/96-Estt.(Res)), an 'Own Merit Candidate' or 'Meritorious Reserved Candidate' (MRC) is a candidate belonging to a reserved category (SC, ST, OBC, or EWS) who secures selection purely on the basis of open general merit without availing any concession or relaxed standard at any stage of the recruitment process (such as relaxation in age limit, experience, educational cut-off marks, or examination fees). Such candidates are appointed against the unreserved (UR) points of the reservation roster and are not counted against the quota reserved for their respective categories. This ensures that the reserved quota remains entirely available for other reserved category candidates.

questions.question_english: The Government of India launched a nationwide flagship campaign to achieve universal accessibility for Persons with Disabilities (PwDs). What is the official name of this campaign?
questions.explanation_english: The Government of India launched the 'Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan' (also known as the Accessible India Campaign) on 3rd December 2015, on the occasion of the International Day of Persons with Disabilities. Executed by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, this flagship initiative aims to create a universally accessible, barrier-free environment across three key verticals: (1) Built Environment Accessibility (retrofitting public buildings, schools, and hospitals with ramps, grab bars, and accessible toilets); (2) Transportation System Accessibility (enhancing accessibility in railways, civil aviation, and state road transport); and (3) Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Ecosystem (making government portals and media accessible to screen-reader users).

questions.question_english:
Consider the following components of school infrastructure:
I. Ramps with handrails
II. Accessible toilets
III. Tactile pathways
Which of the components given above are essential requirements for a barrier-free school environment according to accessibility norms?
questions.explanation_english: Creating an inclusive, barrier-free school environment under the RPwD Act, 2016 (Sections 16 & 40) and the Harmonised Guidelines requires all three components: (I) Ramps with continuous double-tier handrails (at heights of 750 mm and 900 mm) and a standard 1:12 gradient ensure smooth, independent vertical mobility for students using wheelchairs, crutches, or walkers; (II) Accessible unisex toilets with wide sliding or outward-swinging doors, grab bars, low-height washbasins, and emergency call buttons ensure privacy, safety, and hygiene; (III) Tactile ground indicators (guiding and warning pavers) enable visually impaired students to orient themselves, locate entrances, and navigate school corridors safely without risk of collision or falls. Hence, I, II, and III are all essential requirements.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 16 व 40 तथा समेकित दिशा-निर्देशों (Harmonised Guidelines) के अनुसार, बाधा-मुक्त विद्यालय परिवेश के निर्माण हेतु तीनों घटक अनिवार्य हैं: (I) मानक 1:12 ढलान और दोनों तरफ 750 मिमी व 900 मिमी पर दोहरी रेलिंग वाले रैंप व्हीलचेयर और बैसाखी का उपयोग करने वाले विद्यार्थियों के निर्बाध आवागमन को सुनिश्चित करते हैं; (II) चौड़े दरवाजों, ग्रैब बार्स और उपयुक्त ऊंचाई वाले सेनेटरी फिटिंग्स से युक्त सुगम शौचालय शारीरिक दिव्यांग विद्यार्थियों की स्वच्छता व गरिमा सुनिश्चित करते हैं; तथा (III) स्पर्शनीय पाथवे (Tactile pathways/pavers) दृष्टिबाधित विद्यार्थियों को विद्यालय परिसर, गलियारों और सीढ़ियों पर सुरक्षित व स्वतंत्र रूप से आवागमन करने में सहायता करते हैं। अतः I, II और III तीनों अनिवार्य हैं।

questions.question_english: To oversee the implementation of employment reservation provisions and ensure a discrimination-free environment under the RPwD Act, 2016, what specific administrative role must be designated within Government establishments?
questions.explanation_english: Section 23 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 explicitly mandates that every government establishment shall appoint a Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) and inform the Chief Commissioner or the State Commissioner of such appointment. Under Section 23(2), any person aggrieved by non-compliance with the provisions of Section 20 (non-discrimination in employment and provision of reasonable accommodation) may submit a complaint to the Grievance Redressal Officer. The officer is legally obligated to investigate the grievance and take remedial action within two weeks. The GRO also maintains a register of complaints to ensure institutional accountability in government schools and departments.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 23 के अनुसार, प्रत्येक सरकारी प्रतिष्ठान के लिए एक 'शिकायत निवारण अधिकारी' (Grievance Redressal Officer - GRO) नियुक्त करना तथा इसकी सूचना मुख्य आयुक्त या राज्य आयुक्त को देना कानूनी रूप से अनिवार्य है। धारा 23(2) के तहत, यदि किसी दिव्यांग कर्मचारी के साथ धारा 20 के प्रावधानों (रोजगार में भेदभाव का निषेध, उचित समायोजन और पदोन्नति में बाधा) का उल्लंघन होता है, तो वह शिकायत निवारण अधिकारी के समक्ष शिकायत दर्ज करा सकता है। इस अधिकारी को शिकायत प्राप्त होने के दो सप्ताह (14 दिन) के भीतर जांच कर उपचारात्मक कार्रवाई करनी होती है।

questions.question_english: Under Section 21 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, every establishment is statutorily mandated to notify and publish a formal document detailing its measures to provide a barrier-free, supportive, and non-discriminatory environment. What is this official document called?
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 21(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, read with Rules 8 and 9 of the RPwD Rules, 2017, every establishment (including educational institutions, autonomous bodies, and government departments) is legally mandated to notify and publish an 'Equal Opportunity Policy' (EOP). This policy must detail the infrastructure, reasonable accommodations, barrier-free access, non-discriminatory recruitment, assistive technologies, and grievance redressal mechanisms provided to persons with disabilities. Furthermore, a copy of the Equal Opportunity Policy must be formally registered with the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (at the Central level) or the State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (at the State level). It also must be displayed prominently on the establishment's website or notice board.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार (RPwD) अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 21(1) तथा दिव्यांगजन अधिकार नियमावली, 2017 के नियम 8 व 9 के अनुसार, प्रत्येक प्रतिष्ठान (जिसमें शैक्षणिक संस्थान, स्वायत्त निकाय तथा सरकारी विभाग सम्मिलित हैं) को एक 'समान अवसर नीति' (Equal Opportunity Policy) अधिसूचित और प्रकाशित करना अनिवार्य है। इस नीति में दिव्यांग व्यक्तियों के लिए बाधामुक्त बुनियादी ढांचा, उचित आवास (Reasonable Accommodation), गैर-भेदभावपूर्ण भर्ती व पदोन्नति, सहायक उपकरण एवं शिकायत निवारण तंत्र के प्रावधानों का पूरा ब्यौरा दर्ज होना चाहिए। इसके अतिरिक्त, इस नीति की एक प्रति मुख्य आयुक्त अथवा राज्य दिव्यांगता आयुक्त के पास पंजीकृत कराना अनिवार्य होता है तथा इसे संस्थान की वेबसाइट या सूचना पट्ट पर प्रदर्शित किया जाना चाहिए। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।
